{{nihongo|'''Take Minato Jinja'''|多祁御奈刀弥神社|たけみなとみじんじゃ}}, also rendered '''Tagimitonotoya Shrine''' and '''Takeminatomi Shrine''', is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]], located in Ura-shō, Aza Suwa, {{ill|Ishii, Tokushima|ja|石井町}}, [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]], Tokushima Prefecture, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社}} (specifically a {{ill|Shikinai Shosha|ja|式内小社|simple|Shikinai Shosha|qid=Q134917287|lt=Shikinai Shōsha}}) and is regarded as an ancestral shrine of {{ill|Suwa-taisha|ja|諏訪大社}}.

== History ==
The year of the shrine's founding is unknown. The current shrine building was constructed in {{ill|1720|ja|享保}} ({{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 5).

The shrine was highly revered by the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|ja|蜂須賀氏}}, feudal lords of the {{ill|Tokushima Domain|Q3034557|qid=Q3034557}}. During its annual grand festival, members of the clan would often personally visit or send representatives. In {{ill|1627|ja|寛永}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} 4), {{ill|Hachisuka Mitsutaka|ja|蜂須賀光隆}} prayed at the shrine and reported miraculous occurrences. Additionally, because visits by the Hachisuka could be blocked by flooding of the {{ill|Akui River|Q11674107|qid=Q11674107}}, a division of the shrine's spirit was transferred to {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)}} near {{ill|Tokushima Castle|ja|徳島城}} for easier access during times when flooding prevented direct visits to Take Minato Jinja.

According to the shrine's historical records (''Ura-shō Village History''), "In the tenth year of {{ill|Hōki|ja|宝亀}} during the reign of Emperor {{ill|Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇}} (779 CE), the Suwa Daimyōjin of Nakata District, Awa Province, was transferred and enshrined at the Minato Shrine in Suwa, {{ill|Shinano Province|Q289250|qid=Q289250}} (modern-day {{ill|Suwa-taisha|ja|諏訪大社}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}})." This implies that {{ill|Takeminakata no Mikoto|ja|建御名方命}}, known for his mythological dispute with {{ill|Takemikazuchi|ja|武御雷神}} in the kuni-yuzuri episode, originally hailed from Awa Province, and that Suwa Taisha's origins trace back to Awa, as recorded in the shrine's documents.<ref>Sasada Takashi, *The Imperial Capital Yamato was Awa*, Sun Lotus Research Institute, 2024, pp. 173-185.</ref>

== Access ==
* Approximately a 25-minute walk from {{ill|Shimoura Station|ja|下浦駅}} on the {{ill|Tokushima Line|ja|徳島線}} ({{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|Q496531|qid=Q496531|lt=JR Shikoku}}).
* Approximately a 20-minute walk from {{ill|Ushijima Station|ja|牛島駅}} on the same line.

'''Tagimitonotoya Shrine''' (たけみなとみじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} enshrined in Ura-shō, Aza Suwa, {{ill|Ishii, Tokushima|Q1205943|qid=Q1205943}}, {{ill|Myōzai District, Tokushima|Q1155732|qid=Q1155732}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|Q160734|qid=Q160734}}. It is a candidate shrine for the shikinaisha Take-minatone Shrine. There is also a theory that it is the original shrine of {{ill|Suwa-taisha|Q218813|qid=Q218813}}.

=== History ===
The founding year is unknown. The current shrine building was constructed in {{ill|1720|Q6908|qid=Q6908}} ({{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 5).

It was deeply revered by the Hachisuka family, lords of the {{ill|Tokushima Domain|Q3034557|qid=Q3034557}}, who worshiped in person or by proxy at the annual grand festival. In {{ill|1627|Q6833|qid=Q6833}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} 4), {{ill|Hachisuka Mitsutaka|Q3125458|qid=Q3125458}} prayed and reportedly received auspicious signs. It is also said that because visits by the Hachisuka could be blocked by flooding of the {{ill|Akui River|Q11674107|qid=Q11674107}}, a divided spirit was enshrined at {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|Q11631927|qid=Q11631927|lt=Suwa Shrine}} near {{ill|Tokushima Castle|Q8011246|qid=Q8011246}}.

According to the shrine’s traditional record, “in Hōki 10 (779), under {{ill|Emperor Kōnin|ar|الإمبراطور كونين|arz|الامبراطور كونين|azb|کونین (ایمپیراتور)|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆنین|cs|Kónin|de|Kōnin|es|Kōnin Tennō|eu|Kōnin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور کونین|fi|Kōnin|fr|Kōnin|hu|Kónin japán császár|id|Kaisar Kōnin|it|Kōnin|ja|光仁天皇|ko|고닌 천황|mn|Эзэн Хаан Коонин|mr|कोनिन|nl|Konin (keizer)|pl|Kōnin|pt|Konin|ru|Император Конин|sh|Car Kōnin|simple|Emperor Kōnin|sl|Cesar Konin|sv|Kōnin|th|จักรพรรดิโคนิง|tl|Emperador Kōnin|tr|Kōnin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Конін|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōnin|yo|Emperor Kōnin|zh|光仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Kônin Thian-hông|qid=Q958662}}, Minamikatotomi Shrine in Suwa District, {{ill|Shinano Province|Q289250|qid=Q289250}} (today’s {{ill|Suwa-taisha|Q218813|qid=Q218813}} in {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}) transferred and enshrined Suwa Daimyōjin from Myōkata District, {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|Q907457|qid=Q907457}}” (''Ura-shō Village History''). In other words, this record preserves a view that the original base of Takeminakata, who contended with {{ill|Takemikazuchi|lt=Takemikazuchi|Q1502690|qid=Q1502690}} in the kuni-yuzuri episode, was in Awa, and that Suwa Taisha in Nagano was invited from Awa after the compilation of the Kiki<ref>Sasada Takashi, ''The Imperial Capital Yamato Was Awa'', Sun Lotus Research Institute, 2024, pp.173-185.</ref>.
